Sotherly Hotels Inc. ((XBRL-distressed), tier xbrl_distress)
THESIS: The XBRL distress flag is REAL, not an artifact — but it is already-realized history, not a forward mispricing. Pre-merger Sotherly was a chronically over-leveraged post-COVID hotel REIT: ~$315.8M debt (June 30, 2025) at 5.89% WACD against trough EBITDA, producing interest coverage ~0.7x (EBIT ~$15.6M < interest) and net-debt/EBITDA in the mid-teens — i.e. operating earnings could not service interest. Equity was a sliver (shareholder equity ~$36.8M, negative tangible book ~-$3.20/sh) on a ~$320M debt stack (D/E ~870%), and the company had stacked-up preferred dividend arrears (~$23.9M; Series B/C/D dividends deferred Oct/Nov 2025 and future dividends suspended). A hotel-level loan default (SOHO Atlanta LLC, ~$38.0M, lender Wilmington Trust threatening foreclosure) and ~$87.8M of near-term balloon maturities against only ~$9.4M unrestricted cash made the capital structure non-self-financing. The distress resolved through a control event rather than a default cascade: KW Kingfisher LLC (Kemmons Wilson Hospitality Partners + Ascendant Capital JV) acquired the common for $2.25/share on Feb 12, 2026, refinancing with a NEW $308M Apollo senior loan (matures ~2029) plus up to $45M Ascendant mezzanine (matures ~2030) — i.e. leverage was re-struck, not deleveraged. NET: confirm distress = TRUE; forward fragility trade = LARGELY EXHAUSTED. The common is extinguished; the SOHON Series D preferred had a change-of-control conversion right at $16.642013/share cash (conversion date Mar 20, 2026; ~820,066 Series D shares tendered for ~$13.65M on Mar 25, 2026) and the preferred is being voluntarily delisted from Nasdaq to OTC (Form 25 ~Apr 7, 2026) while the company continues SEC reporting. Residual fragility now sits at the asset/loan level inside the new Apollo/Ascendant-financed private vehicle, not in tradeable SOHO/SOHON securities.

System1, Inc. ((XBRL-distressed), tier xbrl_distress)
THESIS: CONFIRMED real distress, not a data artifact — but the canary has already fired AND been partially defused, so the residual mispricing is about execution/dilution, not an imminent surprise default. The economy-wide scan got the direction right but the magnitudes wrong in a way that matters: it reported "near-term (<=2027) debt ~$0.00B," which is the opposite of the truth. At 12/31/2025 essentially the ENTIRE debt stack was near-term — a ~$260M term loan maturing July 2027 and a $50M revolver maturing Jan 27, 2027 (gross principal ~$305M, total debt net $305.1M = $76.7M current + $228.4M LT). That is a 2027 maturity wall against only $86.9M cash and $3.0M net working capital. The XBRL trigger (net-debt/EBITDA ~11.3x, interest coverage ~0.37x) is directionally real but uses a trough/GAAP-style EBITDA of ~$20M; on management's Adjusted EBITDA of $41.9M, cash interest coverage is ~1.5x ($41.9M AdjEBITDA / $27.6M interest) — thin but not zero. The genuine fragility drivers are: (1) revenue in structural decline (FY25 revenue -23% to $266.1M; Q4 -31%), driving (2) an explicit auditor/management going-concern (10-K filed 3/11/2026, doubt for the 12 months following), and (3) extreme counterparty concentration — Google service agreements = 67% of FY25 revenue, a single-point-of-failure for a search-arbitrage model already pressured by AI-driven changes to search. Net loss was $81.2M in FY25. The key update the scan did not capture: on 5/29/2026 System1 executed a distressed debt exchange with ALL term/revolver lenders, swapping ~$302.6M of 2027-maturity debt for a $150M term loan due Jan 2031 (SOFR+5%), $39.3M of convertible preferred (7% PIK-able cumulative dividend), and a ~$31.4M cash payment — cutting indebtedness >$160M and pushing the maturity wall out to 2031. So the 2027 cliff is being termed-out, but at the cost of (a) heavy equity dilution via the convertible preferred (subject to a shareholder vote, close expected Q3 2026), (b) a ~$31.4M cash drain at a company with only ~$87M cash, and (c) an unresolved litigation overhang: certain lenders are suing over the August 2024 reorganization (assets dropped into System1 Holdings LLC) as a potential fraudulent transfer/conveyance — a contingent liability the exchange is partly intended to settle but which is not fully extinguished. Net read: this is an already-distressed micro-cap (S&P CCC+/negative, prior "SD"/selective-default after a distressed buyback), correctly flagged. It is NOT mispriced as a hidden short — the market and ratings already reflect distress. The residual fragility is binary execution risk on the exchange closing + dilution, plus the structural risk that the Google-dependent revenue base keeps shrinking faster than the new $150M/SOFR+5% loan can be serviced (interest alone ~$11-12M/yr on the new loan vs. AdjEBITDA $41.9M and falling).

Mobile Infrastructure Corp ((XBRL-distressed), tier xbrl_distress)
THESIS: CONFIRMED real distress, but the fragility fulcrum is NOT what the scan saw. The scan's "near-term (<=2027) debt ~$0.00B" is a DATA ARTIFACT: it missed the ~$25.9M Harvest Small Cap Partners related-party Line of Credit because its maturity has been serially rolled in 3-month increments (Sept 2025 -> Dec 31 2025 -> Mar 31 2026 -> June 30 2026), so on any given filing date it never reads as a fixed 2026/2027 maturity. THAT LOC is the actual canary. As of Q1 2026: ~$25.9M principal + ~$5.9M accrued interest at a punitive 15.0% PIK-style rate (paid only at maturity) against just $8.5M cash. Management's own 10-K/10-Q carry an explicit 'substantial doubt about the ability to continue as a going concern' — they state they 'do not currently have sufficient cash on hand, liquidity or projected cash flows to repay' the LOC, and assert (probable, not certain) that asset sales + further extension alleviate it. The XBRL coverage/leverage flags are also genuine, not a pure non-cash artifact: even on Adjusted EBITDA (~$14.3M FY25) vs ~$19M interest expense, coverage is only ~0.75x, and on GAAP it is ~0.11-0.57x. The company is cash-burning (FY25 net loss $23.7M, widening; Q1'26 net loss $7.8M) and must sell properties on an 'orderly basis' to service a short-dated related-party balloon. Mitigants that argue AGAINST acute blow-up risk: (1) the LOC lender is an insider affiliate (Jeffrey Osher / No Street Capital), which makes another extension highly likely rather than a hard default; (2) ~$382M total assets / ~$159M equity provide asset coverage and the $100M, 36-month asset-rotation program is funding paydowns (e.g., Honolulu garage sold $16.5M -> $8.1M CMBS + $4.5M LOC paydown); (3) the bulk of debt — $75.5M CMBS at ~4.15% and the $100M ABS at 4.15% (anticipated repayment 2030, legal final 2055) — is genuinely termed out to 2030, so there is no large term-debt wall. Net read: a thinly-capitalized, cash-burning micro-cap whose solvency hinges on (a) continued goodwill of a related-party lender and (b) successful asset sales into a held-for-sale program. Real distress, small dollars (~$0.19-0.21B total debt), and fully self-disclosed — a confirmed canary, not a hidden mispricing.

Xerox Holdings Corp ((XBRL-distressed), tier xbrl_distress)
THESIS: CONFIRMED real distress — NOT a data artifact, though the headline 18.4x net-debt/EBITDA overstates it. The flag was triggered off a trough-EBITDA period (~$0.18B), and ~$1.4B of the ~$4.4B total debt is self-liquidating finance-asset debt (the captive lessor funds customer equipment leases at ~7:1 against ~$1.4B of finance receivables) that should not be levered against operating EBITDA. The honest read is core/operating-company debt of ~$3.0B against ~$500M run-rate EBITDA = ~6-7x core leverage (mgmt and Moody's both peg ~6-7x pro forma). That is still severe. The thesis is corroborated independently of any XBRL ratio by HARD distress events: (1) Moody's downgraded XRX three notches to Caa2 (negative outlook) on weak post-Lexmark performance and refinancing risk; (2) S&P downgraded to 'SD' (selective default) with the 2028 notes cut to 'D' after Xerox repurchased ~$101M face of 2028 notes for ~$45M — a completed below-par/distressed exchange where noteholders got less than promised; (3) a 13% senior bridge note ($125M, due end Q2 2026) is a penalty-rate instrument signaling stressed access to capital; (4) two consecutive years of ~$1B GAAP net losses (FY24 -$1.32B incl. $1.0B goodwill impairment; FY25 -$1.03B); (5) operating cash flow collapsed $511M→$224M FY24→FY25 and went NEGATIVE in Q1 2026 (-$144M OCF, -$165M FCF); (6) the dividend was slashed from $0.125/qtr to $0.025/qtr in 2025 to preserve cash for debt paydown. The genuine question is not whether XRX is fragile (it is, and rating agencies agree) but whether the ~$300M of near-term (≤2027) maturities are manageable — they are bridgeable via the TPG Angelo Gordon IP-JV ($400M+ liquidity) and $637M cash, so the acute risk is the larger $649M 2028 / $500M 2029 wall against a shrinking, FCF-negative core that may force a broader restructuring before 2028. The scan's '≤2027 ~$0.00B near-term' figure is WRONG — there is ~$300M due through 2027 including the 13% bridge.

MERCER INTERNATIONAL INC. ((XBRL-negEBITDA), tier neg_ebitda_levered)
THESIS: CONFIRMED genuine distress, and materially WORSE than the seed screen implied. The XBRL flag was anchored on the stale 2023 down-cycle (net loss $242M, Op. EBITDA ~$17.5M); the company sharply recovered in 2024 (Op. EBITDA $243.7M, positive net income), which would have argued "cyclical one-off." But the relevant fact is the SUBSEQUENT collapse: FY2025 Operating EBITDA went to NEGATIVE $22.0M (Q3-25 alone was -$28.1M), net loss $497.9M including $238.7M of impairments (notably $203.5M writing down the Peace River mill — a tacit admission an asset is structurally uneconomic). The dividend was paused in Q3-2025 to conserve cash. Against ~$1.6B gross debt and an asset base whose cash generation has evaporated, leverage is unmeasurable on negative EBITDA; agencies model debt/EBITDA >10x in 2025 and >6.5x through 2026 even on a recovery. This is a classic "levered cyclical caught at the trough with a wall of refinancing" — the fragility is REAL, not a data artifact, and is now in active pre-restructuring. The seed's "max coupon n/a" is itself a miss: the company already refinanced its old 5.50% 2026 notes into 12.875% 2028 notes — a penalty/distress coupon that is a direct market signal of impaired access.
